text:
maria_cs: Heads-up — AcmePay submitted an escalation 30m ago: model outputs changed after the v2.3 rollout this morning. They say payment descriptions now include extraneous bank routing text and some safety-related rejections have increased. They provided repro steps and a sample convo.

sam_engineering: Can you paste the sample and repro steps here? Need to see if it's prompt-triggered or a model param change.

maria_cs: Paste from customer: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-2.3",
  "input": "Generate a concise payment description for transaction id 99-AB123",
  "temperature": 0.2
}
```
Response includes: "Wire routing number: 021000..." which was never in their prior outputs. They claim same request to redwood-2.2 returns the cleaned description.

leo_ml: Noted. Two quick hypotheses: (1) tokenizer/decoder change in 2.3 that surfaces training artifact tokens, (2) a new safety filter shift causing different post-processing. I’ll diff the decoding config.

caroline_support: Also FYI HealthSync reported similar drift on clinical note summaries — more parenthetical legal phrasing that customers find noisy. Might be a release-wide prompt tuning artifact.

sam_engineering: If it’s model parameterized (e.g., new top_p defaults) that could explain it. Maria, did they set top_p/temperature explicitly? Customer showed temp=0.2 only. No top_p. 2.2 probably had internal gen defaults that matched their expectations.

maria_cs: Correct — they only set temperature. They also said they didn't touch system prompts.

leo_ml: Quick repro on our side: running same payload against stage-2.3 we see the same extraneous routing fragment in ~12% of inferences for short payment prompts. Confirmed.

ashley_prodops: Ops note — we have a canary flag `model:v2.3-routed` that can be toggled per-customer. Suggest routing affected customers back to `redwood-2.2` while we investigate. We can flip per-account via account routing rules in the console.

maria_cs: I'll propose rollback to AcmePay and HealthSync. Drafting comms now. Any reason we shouldn't fallback?

sam_engineering: No blocker. But we should collect telemetry and a small sample set to help ML debug. Do not delete 2.3 until ML confirms. Also capture full requests, infer-time params, and seeds.

leo_ml: Action items for us: 1) diff decoding/postproc between v2.2 and v2.3, 2) run targeted evals with same prompts, 3) inspect tokenizer changes and safety postprocessors. ETA 4 hours for initial triage.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: triggered rollback job for account AcmePay -> routing rule updated to redwood-2.2 (job id: db-7781).

caroline_support: Customer update sent to AcmePay: "We're routing your traffic back to the previous model variant (redwood-2.2) while our engineering team investigates. You should see consistent outputs within minutes. We'll follow up with a root cause and timeline." They replied: "Thanks. Please prioritize — this affects recon reports."

maria_cs: Template I used (feel free to reuse):
"Hi <Acct> — we’ve detected an output change after a recent model rollout. We have routed your traffic to your prior model version as a temporary mitigation. Our engineers are investigating the root cause and we will share updates within 4 hours. If you need a dedicated rollback longer-term, we can schedule it. Apologies for the disruption."

sam_engineering: For short-term mitigations: options we can give customers: 1) Route to previous model, 2) Set `temperature: 0` or lower (reduces hallucinations), 3) Use system prompt override to explicitly sanitize fields (e.g., "Do not include routing numbers or bank details"), 4) Post-filtering on our side for regexes. Provide code snippet: 
```
# recommend low-temp override
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.3","input":"...","temperature":0.0}'
```
Note: temperature 0 is deterministic-ish but may reduce variability required by some customers.

leo_ml: We also found a reproduction that isolates the issue to the decoding tail: in some responses the model emits a token prefix that looks like masked routing metadata. Quick mitigation (internal): add a postprocessor to scrub token sequences matching banking patterns for the next few hours while we patch. Will coordinate with prodops.

ashley_prodops: Can add an on-the-fly postfilter at the gateway for accounts opted-in. Need explicit approval for PII pattern filters — legal already looped in.

maria_cs: Legal OK for regex-based redaction for banking numbers for affected customers. Caroline, can you update support doc and the incident tracker with the mitigation options?

caroline_support: On it. Adding notes to incident board and sending a short FAQ to AcmePay and HealthSync with steps to request extended rollback.

ops-bot: monitoring-bot: created alert rule: increased hallucination-rate for model redwood-2.3 (threshold 5% above baseline).

leo_ml: Follow-ups: 1) if tokenizer or prompt tuning caused it we will prepare a 2.3.1 patch that reverts the offending change, 2) if postproc safety shift, revert config and re-run canary. We’ll post RCA draft within 48 hours.

maria_cs: Customer-facing update I'll send in 2h: short summary + mitigation + ETA for RCA. Any objections?

sam_engineering: Sounds good. Also flagging internal billing/auth check: some customers noted 401s earlier; unrelated but a couple of retries overlapped with rollouts. Ops to confirm no keys rotated for these accounts during the window.

ashley_prodops: Confirmed — no key rotations. 401 spike correlated with a transient auth cache miss in region eu-west-1 at 09:17, unrelated to model rollout. Resolved by cache warm; logged in incident tracker.

maria_cs: Thanks all. I'll proceed with rollback for affected accounts, send the 2h update, and attach the sample set for ML. Please tag me when you have the initial triage.

acme_integration: (from customer) Appreciate the quick action. Would like a follow-up call after RCA.

maria_cs: We'll schedule that — thanks.

sam_engineering: Closing loop checklist: capture 500 failing examples, preserve logs for 14 days, maintain redirection to 2.2 until ML signs off, and add per-route canary control in console UI so CS can flip for specific customers without an ops ticket. Filing a product feature request now.

maria_cs: Added the product request and linked this thread. Keeping this open until initial RCA is posted.

ops-bot: status-bot: thread status -> open (severity: medium, impacted_customers: [AcmePay, HealthSync], mitigation: rollback to 2.2).
